exoplanet_discovery_history: The first confirmed exoplanets were found around a pulsar in 1992. In 1995, astronomers confirmed 51 Pegasi b around a Sun-like star. Thousands of worlds are now known, from small rocky planets to gas giants. Explore how their light reveals them.
transit_geometry_miss: No transit: the planet passes outside the star disc.
transit_geometry_grazing: Grazing transit: only part of the planet crosses the star disc.
transit_geometry_occultation: Complete occultation: the larger planet can cover the entire star.
transit_geometry_full: Full transit: the planet disc passes completely across the star.
transit_scene_label: Planet crossing the star, seen by an observer
transit_intro_linked: Watch a planet block a little starlight. The moving point on the light curve shows the same moment as the planet in the crossing view. Try a larger planet, a smaller star, or a path near the edge.
transit_trappist_source: Published radii: planet 0.920 Earth radii; star 0.1192 Sun radii (Agol et al., 2021). This model uses a chosen central path and does not reproduce the observed light curve.
transit_example_source: Explore a chosen geometry. Earth / Sun and Jupiter-size / Sun are size comparisons; TRAPPIST-1 e loads published planet and star radii.
transit_scene_legend: Gold: star. Dark disc: planet at the correct relative radius. The cyan locator ring helps you find small planets; it does not block light.
transit_graph_help: Drag across the chart, or focus it and use arrow keys. Home goes to the start; End goes to the finish. Time is normalized, not measured in hours.
transit_full_scale_note: Fixed scale: small dips may look flat. The readout still shows the full precision.
transit_zoom_note: Vertical scale adjusts to reveal the dip. Compare the numbers when changing examples.
transit_playback_note: Playback stops at the end. Changing geometry pauses it.
transit_units_help: ppm means parts per million: 10,000 ppm is a 1% brightness drop. Impact parameter is the closest projected separation in star radii: 0 crosses the center; 1 passes along the edge.
transit_limits_heading: What this model can tell you
transit_limits_geometry: This idealized curve uses circular, opaque discs, a uniform-brightness star and constant projected speed. For a small planet fully in front of the star, the fractional dip is (planet radius / star radius)². Grazing crossings block less light.
transit_limits_detection: A dip alone does not guarantee detection. Real measurements depend on stellar brightness and variability, instrument noise, observing cadence and repeated transits. Limb darkening, starspots, atmospheres and measurement noise are omitted here.
